explanation: The site usually identified as Troy, Hisarlik in north-west Anatolia, holds layers of cities built over thousands of years. Heinrich Schliemann began digging there in 1871.

claims.text: In Greek legend, Troy fell after Greek soldiers hid inside a wooden horse.
In the legend, the wooden horse was not used against Sparta, Mycenae or Thebes.
Hisarlik, in north-west Anatolia, is the site usually identified as Troy.
Hisarlik holds the remains of many cities built one on top of another over thousands of years.
Heinrich Schliemann began excavating at Hisarlik in 1871.

evidence.summaryExcerpt: Some give 1870 as the start of his excavations at Hisarlik. Britannica's biography says he began his work there in 1871, digging through the upper levels of the mound. Britannica's Hisarlık entry gives a range, between 1870 and 1890, when Schliemann undertook his own excavations.

claimResults.note: The sources disagree on the start year: Britannica's biography says 1871, while its Hisarlık entry and other sources put the start in 1870 (his first trial trench was dug in April 1870). A conflict fails the claim as written (§9.5.2).

issues.note: c5 (explanation 'Heinrich Schliemann began digging there in 1871'): sources split between 1870 (first trial trench) and 1871 (first full season). Rewrite to what all sources agree on, such as 'began digging there in the early 1870s' or 'in 1870'.

evidence.summaryExcerpt: Some sources say Schliemann began digging at Hisarlik in 1870, but the permit came in 1871, and some sources say the 1870 work was unauthorized. Most sources date the main dig to autumn 1871.

claimResults.note: Sources conflict: Schliemann began digging at Hisarlik in April 1870, without a permit, and his first permitted season was in 1871, so 'began in 1871' depends on which start is counted. A claim on which sources disagree fails as written; 'in the early 1870s' is true on either count.

issues.note: 'Heinrich Schliemann began digging there in 1871' conflicts with sources that date his start to 1870, when he dug without a permit; 1871 is the first permitted season. Say 'in the early 1870s' or 'from 1870'.
